retarder.name: Half-wave retarder film
retarder.desc: The windshield reflects s-polarised light (perpendicular to the plane of incidence) 19 times better than p. The panel already emits linearly polarised light, but its axis may sit at 45° to the edges. A half-wave film rotates that axis to s at no cost in brightness.
retarder.working: A half-wave film mirrors the polarisation about its fast axis: output angle = 2 × fast axis − input, so a 45° input with the fast axis at 67.5° leaves at 90°, which is s at the windshield.
retarder.mount: centre of the film's underside, laid over the crop
facts: output angle = 2 × fast-axis angle − input angle
the measured panel axis is not already along s (Phase 5)

concaveMirror.name: Custom concave relay mirror, 300 × 200 mm, f = 330 mm
concaveMirror.desc: The one custom optic. With the panel 316 mm away, inside its 330 mm focal length, the mirror forms a magnified virtual image 7.5 m behind itself, which the windshield folds into the driver's view. Used 15.5° off axis, a plain sphere splits that image into two focal distances; a toroid with different radii in the two planes brings them together.
concaveMirror.working: A panel point sends a fan of rays that leave the mirror diverging, as if from a point 7.5 m behind it; in a second phase, parallel sunlight from the windshield is focused to a 6 mm spot just past the panel.
concaveMirror.mount: mirror vertex at geom.MIRROR_C; car-frame orientation (normal geom.MIRROR_N, axes geom.MIRROR_U lateral, geom.MIRROR_V tangential)

Its inner surface reflects about a quarter of the s-polarised image toward the eye; the outer surface reflects a second, parallel copy offset by 3.1 mm. targetBoard.name: 30 m registration target board
targetBoard.desc: A surveyed target set 30 m in front of the car. The road camera detects its rings while a camera at the eye point photographs the rendered markers over them; the difference is the registration error.
targetBoard.working: Detected and surveyed markers sit over each ring target; their gap is what the calibration removes.
targetBoard.mount: ground centre under the board; the target face looks toward -X (the car)
facts: refines the nominal eye point (calibration step 1) and checks static registration
static registration at 30 m ≤ 0.5°; ≤ 0.3° under ±75 mm head motion
camera at the eye point vs the surveyed board; marker from the road camera's detection and from the survey
$300 (estimate; plan line "Latency probe, rangefinder, target board", last seen 2026-10-21)

parts.name: Target panel
parts.desc: Matte panel with a checker border and a ruled centre cross.

parts.name: Ring targets
parts.desc: Each centre is surveyed; the road camera detects them too, which separates perception error from optics error.

assembly.title: Panel and targets
assembly.text: Set at 30 m on the car's axis; survey each target with the rangefinder.

rangefinder.name: Handheld laser rangefinder
rangefinder.desc: Surveys distances for calibration: the target board at 30 m and the reference ranges the stereo depth is scored against.
rangefinder.working: The laser spot lands on the target and the range reads out.
rangefinder.mount: centre of the body; it looks along +X
facts: surveys the 30 m target board and range checks for the stereo depth
range within 10% of the stereo median (Phase 1 score)
$300 (estimate; plan line "Latency probe, rangefinder, target board", last seen 2026-10-21)

assembly.title: Optics
